description: Married filing separately, age 67, lived with the spouse during the year: base amount 0, so 85% of the worksheet's line 7 is taxable; no senior deduction on a separate return.
worked:
Filing status: married filing separately, lived with the spouse at some time in the year.
Taxpayer: born 1958-09-02, age 67 at the end of 2025.
Form 1040: lines 4b + 5b taxable pensions and IRA distributions 6,000; line 6a Social Security benefits 20,000.
Social Security Benefits Worksheet (Form 1040 instructions, lines 6a and 6b; Publication 915 Worksheet 1):
  line 1 = 20,000; line 2 = 50% x 20,000 = 10,000
  line 3 (lines 1z, 2b, 3b, 4b, 5b, 7a, 8) = 6,000; line 4 (line 2a) = 0
  line 5 = 10,000 + 6,000 + 0 = 16,000; line 6 (Schedule 1 adjustments) = 0; line 7 = 16,000
  line 8: married filing separately and lived with the spouse, so base amount and adjusted base amount are 0 (IRC 86(c)(1)(C), (c)(2)(C)); skip lines 8-15; line 16 = 85% x 16,000 = 13,600
  line 17 = 85% x 20,000 = 17,000; line 18 = smaller of 13,600 and 17,000 = 13,600 -> Form 1040 line 6b
Form 1040 line 9 total income = 6,000 + 13,600 = 19,600; line 10 adjustments 0; line 11a/11b adjusted gross income = 19,600.
Line 12e standard deduction = 15,750 basic (married filing separately) + 1 x 1,600 additional (married or surviving spouse amount, one per box checked on line 12d for age 65 or older / blind) = 17,350.
Schedule 1-A Part V: not allowed on a married-filing-separately return (a married person must file jointly); senior deduction 0.
Line 14 = 17,350 + 0 = 17,350; line 15 taxable income = 19,600 - 17,350 = 2,250.
Form 1040 line 16 (regular tax): Tax Rate Schedule Y-2 (married filing separately) on 2,250: 10% x 2,250 = 225; total 225
Form 8960: lines 8 and 12 net investment income = 0; line 13 MAGI = 19,600; line 14 threshold = 125,000; line 15 = 19,600 - 125,000, zero or less, so 0; line 17 net investment income tax = 0.
Form 8959: no wages or self-employment income; additional Medicare tax 0.
Total tax = 225 regular + 0 net investment income tax + 0 additional Medicare tax = 225.
